title: Neighbourhoods and module stalks at a singleton finite fibre
statement: Let $\pi:Z\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $z\in Z$, and put $y=\pi(z)$. Suppose $\pi^{-1}(\{y\})=\{z\}$. For every open neighbourhood $U\subseteq Z$ of $z$ there is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq Y$ of $y$ such that $\pi^{-1}(V)\subseteq U$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent], the canonical germ map $(\pi_*\mathcal G)_y\to\mathcal G_z$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules, where the action on $\mathcal G_z$ is through $\pi_z^\sharp:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. Here $(\pi_*\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal G(\pi^{-1}W)$ for open $W\subseteq Y$ with scalars restricted along the structure sheaf map [def-pc-module-pullback], and stalks are as in [def-pc-module-stalk-functor].

proof.text: A finite morphism is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft] and therefore universally closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. Given an open U containing z, take V to be the complement of the closed image of Z minus U. A point outside U mapping to pi(z) must equal z by the singleton-fibre hypothesis, a contradiction. Hence V contains pi(z) and its inverse image lies in U.

proof.text: Use the alternative stalk proof explicitly given at the end of Stacks Tag 05B8. Every element of G_z is the germ of a section s on some U containing z. Step 1 supplies V with inverse image contained in U. Restrict s to this inverse image; its pushforward germ maps to the original germ by stalkPushforward_germ_apply and germ_res_apply. For injectivity represent two pushforward stalk elements on target neighbourhoods U and V. Equality after stalkPushforward means their source sections agree on a neighbourhood W of z, by the filtered-colimit germ_eq criterion. Use Step 1 to obtain Q with inverse image inside W, and intersect Q with U and V. On this intersection the two pushforward sections agree, since restriction maps compose and maps between opens are unique. Thus their germs agree. This proves bijectivity and hence IsIso in AddCommGrpCat, without quasi-coherence.

proof.text: Represent a target-ring stalk scalar by a section r on U, and the pushforward-module stalk element by a section m on a smaller V contained in U. Restrict r to V. The module germ_smul identity identifies their stalk scalar product with the germ of the sectionwise scalar product. The pushforward action on m is multiplication by pi.app(V)(r). Apply stalkPushforward_germ_apply to both module germs, then germ_smul on the source, and Scheme.Hom.germ_stalkMap_apply to the scalar germ. The resulting equality is exactly scalar compatibility along pi.stalkMap(z). This is the canonical map in the original statement; no choice of a stalk isomorphism is made.
